title: CSRF Protection
definition: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF): An attack where a malicious site tricks a user's browser into executing an unwanted action on a site where they are currently authenticated.
simpleExplanation: You are logged into your Bank. You visit `EvilSite.com`. EvilSite secretly sends a POST request to `Bank.com/transfer-money`. Because your browser automatically attaches your Bank cookies, the Bank thinks YOU made the request.
realWorldExample: Preventing CSRF by using `SameSite` cookies, ensuring that the browser ONLY sends cookies if the request actually originates from your own Next.js domain.

basic: What attribute on a browser cookie is the primary defense against CSRF attacks in modern web development?
intermediate: Why do Server Actions in Next.js automatically protect you from CSRF attacks?

answers.question: Server Actions protect?
answers.answer: Next.js Server Actions automatically implement 'Origin Matching'. They compare the `Origin` header of the incoming POST request to the server's actual host name. If they don't match, the request is violently rejected.
